notes.title: Spring Update!
notes.content:
Hello, builders!
It's been a while since last update, but here I am with some news... and some demands.

[h2]New feature: fast travel![/h2]

The main new feature introduced with this update is the possiblity to [b]fast travel[/b] from the map to a bunch of dedicated locations scattered around the main world, in the form of wooden canoes.
It isn't much, but I figured this feature could be useful to avoid skating all the way back to reach an old, unsolved level, or to reach the newly opened bridges towards the extra islands.
Hope you can find this a handy tool!

The [b]visualization of the key rebinding menu[/b] have also been fixed to avoid text overlapping and to remove Italian key names that popped up by default... let me know if it works better now!

And last, the [b]game demo[/b] have received a long due update to match the full game's current state.

[h2]Reviews, reviews, reviews[/h2]

With the humongous amount of wonderful games available on Steam, I am already really grateful someone trusted this little game of mine enough to spend some money on it.
However, if you bought and played the game, it would be wonderful if you could spare a minute to leave a review in the comments section... positive or negative, it doesn't matter! Right now, the game is quite buried in the algorithm depths, so some more positive reviews would help other people find out about it... on the other side, some criticism would help ME understand where I could do a better job in the future!
Thanks in advance to those who will answer this call!

[h2]Discount incoming[/h2]

Last but not least, to "celebrate" the update, the game will be on a discount for a week from now!

notes.title: Positively ready!
notes.content:
[h2]Almost there![/h2]

Winter is coming! Or December is coming, at least, and this means that in five days you'll be able to start Building Your Igloo!
It feels about right that this little adventure, which begun with me learning how to use Unity as a hobby during the pandemic, is getting to the finish line with me being (once again) positive to good ol' Covid 19... luckily with mild inconveniences!

[h2]Credit where it's due[/h2]

With the last uploaded build, I consider the game to be ready for the imminent release... and the main confirm is that the game now has a proper end, with credits and all, instead of the brutal "YOU WIN" message I put as a placeholder.

The other major update is the [b]key rebinding menu[/b]: it is now possible to remap inputs from the keyboard to match your preferences! This is valid for keyboard only, not for controllers.

Last, you may notice a different background music when opening the game. It's not much, but I think it creates a bit of a break, a separation, between the menu and the actual gameplay.

That's it, for today! Have a nice week and... see you on Friday, builders!

notes.title: Achievements unlocked!
notes.content:
Hello, builders!

Only two weeks before you can start building your igloos, but there's still some work to do.
Let me share the latest progresses with you.

[h2]Achievements![/h2]

That's right, How To Build Your Igloo now features [b]15 achievements[/b]! Not many, just the right amount to help you keep track of (and reward) your progresses as you skate through the Puzzle Pole.
So far I've only tested the full functionality of some of them, so if you happen to encounter any trouble with any of the achievements, please let me know!

[h2]Windowed mode[/h2]

I added to the graphic options the possibility of switching between full screen and a windowed mode. This may be useful for some players or could help with slower PCs. The new option has been tested and it looks like it works properly, but again, please report any issue you may encounter.

[h2]New input system[/h2]

Last, I dared to put my hands back on the control scripts (fighting against the "it works fine, let it be") and I managed to successfully switch to Unity's new input system. No difference for you builders, but it should make it easier for me to try and add key rebinding options to the game. This is probably the last feature I'll work on these days, but in all honesty I can't say for sure it will be there at release day: it depends on how easy it will be to implement (considering my little experience too) and on how many troubles it will cause to my poor code!

Stay tuned for more final updates!

Rava

notes.title: Level up!
notes.content:
Hello builders!

The beginning of November brings good news and GREAT news!
Let's hear them!

[h2]TL:DR[/h2]

[list]
[*] Level design completed: the game will feature [b]250 levels![/b]
[*] No, you won't need to solve ALL of them... but I still hope you'll ENJOY doing it!
[*] Last development step: [b]achievements[/b]!
[*] Official release date: [b]December the 1st[/b]!
[/list]

[h2]250 levels![/h2]

That's right! While kids (and grown-ups) were outside playing "Trick or Treat", I've been inside creating the last of the 250 levels that you'll find in How To Build Your Igloo... so, now, I can officially declare the level design process completed! And what a journey!

I'm quite satisfied with how all the levels came out... the hardest part, with so many levels, was to give each one its own personality, wether this personality was in the mechanics involved in the level, in what inspired the level in the first place (you'll find a lot of winks and tributes both in the names and shapes of many levels) or in both sides.
I feel there's no filler levels around the Puzzle Pole, in the end... but it'll be up to you builders to tell me if this is true or not!

If 250 sounds like TOO MANY levels, remember that the whole game is conceived so that the end can be reached solving just half of them! The overabundance of levels is meant to be both a treat for who will enjoy the game (the more you solve, the more you get to play!) and a help for beginners and casual players, who in most situations will be able to skip / work around a particularly hard level or to leave it for a while, moving to different levels / areas without just being stuck (which is something that, in my experience, can be enough to make you rage quit a game).

[h2]Almost done![/h2]

With level and world design behind my back, the game is almost ready for release!
There's still one main task I'm going to tackle this month: the achievements!
As a player, I don't like forced achievements that seem unrelated with the spirit of the game, but I feel there are some key achievements that a puzzle game just needs... the ones which give you certification of your success!

[h2]Release date: minus one month![/h2]

And now to the great news: I feel confident enough with the game development state to announce an official release date: [b]How To Build Your Igloo will be out on Steam on December the 1st![/b]
By the way, there will be a small discount on the full price for the first week, so... save the date!

Rava

notes.title: How To Build Your Igloo @ Steam Next Fest!
notes.content:
[h2]After you tried THAT demo...[/h2]
I know... We've all been waiting for The Talos Principle 2 for SO long that it's now literally stealing the show!
So, when you're done playing that demo, why don't you come and check what the Puzzle Pole has to offer?
Hello, builders, and welcome to [b]How To Build Your Igloo![/b]
Please play the available short demo and share your opinions / feedback! Keep in mind that it only shows the very first, introductory section of the game, which is super easy... but there's also a preview of medium-advanced levels right at the end!
Oh, and if you'll decide to get the full game, you'll be able to carry over your progresses from the demo... no need to replay those tutorial levels!

[h2]Game status update[/h2]
Talking about the game development, I've just designed the [b]230th level[/b] of the game, which means it's only 20 more levels to go!
Some final areas of the Puzzle Pole map are still in progress, but the day this adventure will be available for everyone to play is getting closer and closer.
I'm also learning how to insert [b]achievements[/b], so the final game should have some of those too before release!

Enjoy the Fest and, if you find anything interesting (like this game <wink, wink>), please [b]spread the news![/b]

notes.title: Demo update
notes.content:
Hello builders!

Being a beginner also means learning how things work by making mistakes and correcting them.
This specific update is no big deal, but it impacts whoever has already [b]played the demo[/b].
Let's go into details.

[h2]Demo saving method has changed[/h2]

When releasing HTBYI demo, I stated that [b]progresses from the demo could be carried on to the full game[/b].
During the last week I realised, through some tests, that this [b]wasn't actually the case[/b], because I hadn't fully comprehended how cloud saving and folder organising worked within Steam and Unity.

[h2]Good news: issue fixed![/h2]

A very small modification to the overall settings of the game was enough to [b]fix this issue[/b] and now the full game should be able to find and maintain the demo progresses. And this is good news.

[h2]Bad news: you may have lost your demo progresses[/h2]

Now to the (slightly) bad news: because of this change, if you played the demo [b]before last weekend[/b] (so before the end of September), you may find out that you've lost your saved data for the demo and that you have to restart the game from the beginning.
The demo is short and easy, so I feel it wouldn't be a big deal, but still I feel the need to apologize for this inconvenient... of course, I'll try NOT to cause similar inconveniences once the full game is out! That wouldn't be good for reputation, I guess.

[h2]Good news again (maybe): your progresses could not be completely lost[/h2]
There may be, however, an easy way to recover your lost progresses from the depth of your PC.
If you already played through the demo and you don't want to start over, contact me at soggetto.rava@gmail.com and I'll give you instructions on how to recover the missing savefile.

That's it for the day! Rookie mistakes are called rookie mistakes for a reason... right?

See you in a week for the Steam Next Fest, builders!

Rava

notes.title: Cartographer
notes.content:
[h1]July update![/h1]

Hello, builders!
This is a quick update about the game development state: the Puzzle Pole, the overworld from where the player is going to access all the levels, is now completed! Here's a glimpse of what it looks like:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44188285/96329f89bb846cf2863d2873e7d370f8c8e4f579.gif[/img]

You can't see anything with all those clouds, you say?
Well, of course... I don't want to spoil too much!
But I can tell you I'm quite satisfied about the overworld design and I can also tell you that the final game will consist of as many as 250 levels... which I think is enough too keep you scratching your head for a little while!
But don't worry: the overworld is also designed so that you're not forced to solve ALL levels... most of the times you'll be able to work around any particularly tough level and to proceed anyway towards the end.
Of course, I hope you'll enjoy the game enough to go back and try solving all of the levels! Remember: the more you solve, the more you get access to!

See you on the next update!

Andrea
